Given the strong inbound interest we see for our product, we decided to double down on our next phase of growth, focusing on the US market. If you have not heard of Kayzen before: Kayzen is the Apps DSP: an AI-native platform built on its own bidding engine, for buying app inventory across mobile and connected TV screens. App developers, agencies, media buyers and ad platforms use Kayzen to drive full-funnel outcomes across both screens, from awareness and consideration to installs, purchases and calls. Available through self-serve and managed services, Kayzen combines machine-learning optimisation with bid - and impression-level transparency, granular control over buying decisions, and AI capabilities that connect campaign data to the AI assistants teams already use. Kayzen’s vision is to democratise programmatic marketing by making it accessible to every team. Headquartered in Berlin, Kayzen operates globally. We are a founder-led business, run by a team in which most senior members have at least a decade of experience in the mobile app performance advertising space. We are currently around 90 FTE and keep growing profitably. The Team You will be part of the global leadership team, working with Co-Founders / management and a carefully selected, diverse and globally distributed team of leaders and ICs spanning customer success, marketing, sales & business development, data, product and more functions. We are highly motivated and aligned in our quest to disrupt the multi-billion dollar mobile and CTV ad-tech industry. The Role Your role requires a deep understanding of the advertising technology industry with its various actors, such as advertisers, agencies, ad platforms (DSPs, SSPs, Measurement, etc). Kayzen offers a leading technology platform used by a diverse set of customers (multiple ICPs: Apps, Agencies, Media Buyers) who aim to get performance outcomes from ad campaigns running on CTV and mobile apps. The unifying element of our customers is that they choose Kayzen for our ability to deliver measurable results while giving them full transparency and control. Whether the outcomes they look for are app installs, new customers, purchases and repeat purchases or upper funnel goals like engagement and brand lift. The main geographic market focus of our business is on Europe and the US, though the platform accesses inventory globally. The Kayzen team members you will interact with are primarily based in Europe (soon growing in the US). Responsibilities Work closely with the C-Suite to develop and execute GTM strategies for growing our business in the US Build and maintain strong relationships with industry contacts such as partners, select key customers and suppliers, and multipliers who can help us amplify our reach Build a lean but high performing team that is strongly aligned with our culture and values (for culture and values, see more here: kayzen.io/careers )

Billing is doing the critical work of converting our revenue into cash that we put in the bank. Otherwise, money we cannot collect is money we’ve already burned. jobs.title: Project Sceptrum - Multilingual AI Coding Evaluation Specialist - Dutch
jobs.description: Join a short, paid project that tests whether AI coding agents work as well on instructions written in the target language as they do in English. Your language skills and technical background decide where you fit. About the project Welo Data is helping evaluate how well AI coding agents perform when the instructions they receive are written in languages other than English. Agents are given a real software engineering task in a code repository, and automated tests check whether they solved it. The code, repositories and tests stay exactly as they are. Only the human-written instructions change language, so the quality of every instruction directly affects the result. About the roles There are two roles on this project. We place you in one of them based on your experience & skillsets. Translator: translate English software engineering task briefs into the target language. You keep every requirement, constraint and success condition, and you leave commands, file paths, API names, code and test conditions exactly as written in English. This role suits people with a stronger technical background, and translation experience is a plus. Reviewer: compare each translation with the English source, check that nothing is missing, added or changed in meaning, correct errors, and log each correction by error type. This role suits people with strong translation, editing or review experience and enough technical familiarity to read code context. Who we are looking for Native or near-native writing in the target language, and strong reading ability in English. Either professional experience in translation, editing, review or technical writing, or a software background combined with excellent writing in the target language Comfort reading technical text. Coding experience is a strong plus for the translation role and helpful for the review role. Close attention to detail. In this project, a dropped clause can make a task fail. Project at a glance Project duration: one week since the mid of November Languages: Dutch Project time commitment: 6 hours per person Project compensation: varies depends on different programming language Work location: fully remote How selection works (major steps) Screening questions: about 2 minutes. They cover your language background, translation and review experience, which programming languages you know and how well, and your availability. Language test: short exercises in the target language. Programming skills assessment: you will be invited to another opportunity, in the programming language you know best (Rust, Go, Python, or TypeScript / JavaScript). It confirms your technical level and places you in a language track. Financial Onboarding & Role placement: complete the financial onboarding with Welo Data. In the meanwhile, you will be informed about the decision whether you are placed in the initial translation role or the review role. Production: once you finish all steps above, our project team will contact you for production. Choose when and how much you want to contribute—fully remote, with complete autonomy. 🌱 Limitless Growth Optional access to AI and Large Language Model workshops designed specifically for professionals like you. No coding required—just your expertise. 🌍 Limitless Support Be part of a global contributor community with responsive guidance

Our mission is human wellbeing, and we believe personalised medicine will transform it. Our founding insight is that getting there requires a system that learns continuously from care and its outcomes, optimising for human wellbeing. Building that learning engine is the opportunity at the heart of Anima. We're now in 1,000+ clinics across 5 product lines, serving more than 25% of the UK population. We are cash flow positive, growing fast, and have a tight crew of ~45 people who care deeply for each other and the mission. Everyone has real ownership and a voice in decisions. jobs.description: Background Nash powers the logistics infrastructure behind some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, and 7-Eleven, along with platforms like Shopify and Toast. We are scaling fast, the category is forming around us, and we are building the product marketing function from scratch. We're hiring our first Product Marketing Lead to own positioning, narrative, launches, and the strategic voice of the platform that is becoming foundational to modern commerce. The Role This is the strategic seat where positioning, narrative, customer truth, competitive worldview, and launch craft come together. It is also where the next chapter of Nash's product strategy is shaped. Product marketing can take many different forms in different organizations... It can be a function to spit out whitepapers and datasheets, a megaphone for product management, or… it can be something very different: a force multiplier for the whole organization. We're looking for the latter. You'll report directly to our Chief Growth Officer (whose career has been building and leading marketing, growth, and product organizations at companies like Twilio, Plaid, and Salesforce). You'll work as a peer to our Product Team, and alongside our CEO, our CTO, and a small, senior, fast-moving cross-functional group across product, engineering, sales, and growth. The bar for taste, craft, and strategic thinking on this team is high, and the trajectory for someone strong in this seat is significant. How We Think About PMM The best PMMs sit at the intersection of three rare skills: technical curiosity, business acumen, and creativity. You don't need to be a coder, but you need to understand technical implementation, tradeoffs, and be able to talk to a technical audience credibly enough to know what they'll ask next. You don't need to be a salesperson, but you need to read buying behavior, understand the worldview of the decision-maker, and articulate the value of the problem we're resolving (not the value of our product). You talk in the language of the customer, not the language of our company. You don't need to be a designer or a copywriter, but you need to write narratives with emotional resonance, position with clear differentiation, and find the experiment, the data, or the execution model that actually moves the needle. The skills are hard enough to find in one person. The harder bar is what you do with them. Great PMM teams are not measured on what they did. They are measured on what they got the company to achieve together. They don't ask the org to enable them. They enable the org. They earn strategic influence by inspiring the company with a common vision, and then get the whole company pulling together in the same direction. How We Work: AI-Native, By Default Product marketing at Nash is AI-native and builder-led. We're looking for a PMM who has fundamentally rewired their workflow around AI, not someone who occasionally uses ChatGPT to clean up an email. Someone who reaches for Claude, Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Replit, and whatever ships next week as instinctively as they reach for a Google doc. The reason is straightforward: the speed and surface area of what one product marketer can produce has changed by an order of magnitude in the last eighteen months. Customer interview synthesis, competitive teardowns, narrative iteration, message testing at scale, launch asset production, sales enablement, internal narrative documents: every loop

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist, Audio
jobs.description: Company Overview Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram. Company Operating Rhythm At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance. Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do. Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5. Deepgram is looking for a Data Scientist to sit at the intersection between research and data: people who think deeply about what conversational data is actually composed of, what makes data valuable, and how to best leverage that. Conversational audio presents incredibly rich scientific, engineering, and infrastructure challenges that are orders of magnitude harder than working with text. Speech carries speakers, accents, dialects, emotion, overlapping talk, code-switching, domain vocabulary, and acoustic conditions that range from a quiet studio to a drive-through — all with rich context that moves the conversation. In this role you'll collaborate closely with our research, engineering, and data teams to answer those questions rigorously and at scale. You'll care deeply about what makes conversational data difficult, you'll characterize it, and you'll shape the strategies that turn it into model gains. This role rewards conviction, creativity in approach, and a real appetite for overturning your own assumptions when the data says otherwise. This is a hands-on, high-leverage role with unusual latitude to define an area from first principles. It reports to the VP of Data Operations. We're looking for people who: See "we've always done it this way" as a starting position to argue with, not a constraint to work around Can find the one experiment that settles a question in days rather than months Are creative about where signal hides — in metadata, in model confidence, in the failures Have the vision to take a scrappy proof-of-concept and scale it 100x Are obsessed with using AI to automate and amplify their own impact W

jobs.description: Who we are At Domino, we build solutions that help the largest, highly regulated organizations adopt AI to accelerate mission-critical use cases. In the world of AI today, we believe that the future is still being invented — and we want to be the ones building it. For more information, visit www.domino.ai What we are building Domino’s Identity and Access platform (IDSM) is the foundation for how customers in some of the world’s most regulated industries manage who can see and do what. We’re evolving it into a centralized, relationship-based authorization framework built on SpiceDB, and you’d be the technical anchor for its next phase. A unified authorization model. Extend a centralized, fine-grained, relationship-based model across the platform, replacing feature-specific permission checks with consistent, reusable primitives. Production-grade operations. Harden the authorization layer for the scale, reliability, and security that enterprise and public-sector customers expect. A thoughtful migration path. Make the sequencing and design calls that let us retire legacy access checks without disrupting customers along the way. Groups and organizations that mirror real customers. Rethink how we model groups and organizational hierarchies so large enterprises can represent their teams the way they actually work. Cloud-native identity. Deepen integration with cloud workload identity, starting with AWS IRSA and extending to Azure and GCP equivalents. Foundations other teams build on. Design core identity and access capabilities, with clean interfaces and flexible abstractions, that engineers across the company can adopt with confidence. A stronger way of building. Set the patterns for how the team uses AI-assisted development to ship high-quality features faster, without compromising security or code quality. What your impact will be Set the architectural direction. Design identity and access solutions that meet customer demands for managing user and group access, and are secure, scalable, and built on primitives teams can reuse. Bring clarity to complex decisions. Articulate the architecture clearly enough that the rest of Engineering can rally around it. Be the go-to authority. Engineers and teams building on IDSM will bring their auth questions to you, and your technical judgment will carry real influence. Raise the engineering bar. Lead design reviews, unblock engineers facing ambiguity, and champion flexible abstractions and well-thought-out interfaces. Increase velocity and reduce maintenance. Improve our architecture, including removing tech debt, so the team ships faster with less ongoing maintenance. Shape how we build with AI. Establish patterns for using AI-assisted development to deliver high-quality features faster without compromising security or rigor. Foster ownership

jobs.title: AI Scientist (LATAM)
jobs.description: Build a Safer World. TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure. TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions, including our AI investigations platform Ardence, that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime and global security threats. At TRM, you'll join a mission-driven, fast-paced team made up of experts in law enforcement, data science, engineering, and financial intelligence, tackling complex global challenges daily. As an AI Scientist on our new AI Research team, you will build the models and agents behind the intelligence that powers TRM's products. Part of that is training foundation models on blockchain data, one of our most differentiated data layers, and part is building autonomous AI agents that generate intelligence at a scale hand-built heuristics cannot reach. You'll work on Intel Cortex and other ambitious, cross-cutting ideas, with a broad view across intelligence rather than a single risk category. This is pioneering work that does not exist elsewhere in our industry, and it directly drives customer outcomes, from seizing illicit funds to disrupting criminal networks. The impact you'll have here: Train ML models on blockchain data , including foundation models, and take them from research to production. Build AI agents (and fine-tune LLMs where it helps) so the intelligence underneath TRM's products is generated by models and agents, not only hand-built heuristics. Find new ways to generate net new intelligence , using patterns across all intelligence layers ( Network / On-chain / Protocol ) that competitors can't replicate. Ship production-quality code : ML models, agents and data pipelines, with rigorous evaluation and scalable architecture. Take on ambitious, high-impact bets that raise the ceiling of what our intelligence can do, and drive measurable outcomes: billions in illicit funds traced, seized, or prevented. What we’re looking for: Quantitative background (Computer Science, Statistics, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics). Advanced degree or equivalent research experience is a plus. Strong machine learning foundations , built over years of applied ML and/or research (modeling, evaluation, experimentation). You don't need to have trained a foundation model or built agents before, but you need the fundamentals to do it. Strong problem-solving mindset : gets to the root cause, leverages creativity, and thrives in ambiguity with a hypothesis-driven, iterative approach. 5+ years of hands-on machine learning experience, with strong Python , SQL , and AI-assisted coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code). Experience with distributed data systems ( Spark, BigQuery, Airflow ) and shipping production ML code. Strong async communication (Loom, Slack, Notion), strong technical communication in English, and ability to own work independently in a remote environment. Bonus: experience with LLMs, AI agents or fine-tuning; domain curiosity or prior work in blockchain, crypto, fraud, money laundering or financial crime. About the Team: AI Research is a new team focused on ambitious, cross-cutting ideas in attribution and intelligence. Fully remote and globally distributed. Most overlap occurs 7am

Guided by our mission to make the world’s health data secure, accessible and actionable, we provide critical data solutions for organizations across the healthcare ecosystem - including providers, health plans, researchers, and life sciences companies. From fulfilling a single patient’s request for their medical records to powering the AI revolution in healthcare, Datavanters are building the future of how data is connected and used to improve health. By joining Datavant today, you’re stepping onto a driven and highly collaborative team that is passionate about creating transformative change in healthcare. What We’re Looking For: As a Clinical Documentation Quality Improvement (CDQI) Audit Specialist, you will be instrumental in evaluating the quality, accuracy, compliance and effectiveness of CDI reviews while identifying opportunities for education, process improvement and revenue integrity enhancement. The Auditor provides feedback, education and performance monitoring to support continuous improvement of the CDI program. Join us in this critical role where your efforts will have a direct and meaningful impact on the quality and effectiveness of patient care. This role is full-time. What You Will Do: Conduct retrospective and concurrent audits of CDIQ Specialists work to ensure accurate documentation review practices, compliant query generation, assess appropriate capture of: SOI, ROM, CC/MCC, HCC, and align with coding, quality and regulatory requirements. Review missed opportunities impacting reimbursement, quality reporting and patient outcomes. Collaborate with physicians and caregivers to ensure appropriate reimbursement and clinical severity for DRG-based payer patients. Evaluate CDQI staff adherence to organizational workflows, policies and industry standards. Maintain audit tools, scoring methodologies, and audit documentation Provide individualized feedback to CDQI Specialists and develop education plans based on audit findings. Participate in onboarding and mentoring new CDQI staff. Deliver educational presentations on documentation, coding, regulatory updates and best practices. Collaborate with Physician Advisor regarding documentation opportunities and trends. Monitor program performance indicators, including query rates, query response rates, agreement rates, accuracy scores, case mix index impact and CC/MCC capture rates. Maintain confidentiality and safeguard protected health information (PHI), medical records, audit documentation, and company data in compliance with HIPAA, organizational policies, and regulatory requirements. Adhere to established privacy, security, and information governance standards when accessing, reviewing, storing, and communicating sensitive information. Meet or exceed established production, quality, and performance metrics by completing assigned audits within designated timeframes and maintaining high standards of accuracy, consistency, and objectivity. Produce clear, actionable audit findings and educational feedback that support CDI staff development and program improvement What You Need to Succeed: 5+ years of CDI experience and/or auditing. 3+ years of clinical experience in an academic medical center. jobs.description: Who are we? At UpGuard , we are replacing manual security bottlenecks with AI-driven precision. We build the Cyber Risk Posture Management (CRPM) platform that security teams actually love. By integrating security ratings, threat intel, and agentic AI, we empower organisations to stay ahead of an ever evolving attack surface. We aren’t just building another tool; we’re defining a category. We provide the autonomy to ship world-class technology and the resources to do it at a global scale. Why are we hiring for this role? We're hiring a Lead, Virtual Events & Launch Programs to build and run UpGuard's global digital event and launch programs: Summit, our quarterly product launch broadcast, plus a year round series and on-demand content engine that keeps security and risk leaders engaged between launches. You’ll set the strategy for how we use virtual events to reach security and risk leaders, and run the program that delivers it: webinars, virtual roundtables, and digital event series for audiences in North America, EMEA, and APAC, including our quarterly launch event (Summit), where we showcase what’s new across the UpGuard platform. Build and run UpGuard's speaker program: recruit, brief, coach and rehearse executives, customers, analysts and industry experts, and develop a bench of repeat speakers Brief demand gen, content and design on each event's audience, positioning and assets so promotion lands with the right buyers. Own the virtual event platform end to end, including administration, integration with CRM, data quality and attribution setup, so every registration and attendance is captured and routed correctly Own the KPIs for Summit and our virtual program: registration-to-attendance rate, live and on-demand engagement, post-launch feature awareness and adoption, pipeline from the on-demand library, and attendee and speaker satisfaction. Working hours: M-F, 10AM - 6:30PM Location: Oude Meer, North Holland, 1438 BC Contract: 6 month FTC About Nivoda Nivoda is the leading global B2B jewellery marketplace, Nivoda’s growth trajectory has skyrocketed over the past 12 months, and we continue to expand across new regions at an unprecedented pace. Our DNA centers on understanding our customers' needs and offering them a seamless experience. With a growing team based in major cities worldwide, including London, New York, Hong Kong, and Mumbai, Nivoda is becoming the go-to marketplace for the global jewelry industry. We aim to be bold, innovative, and relentless in our pursuit of excellence as we transform an industry steeped in tradition. The Role As a Junior Fulfilment Executive, you'll be a key player in a tight-knit team. Working alongside highly experienced logistics professionals at one of our largest international hubs, you'll handle and repack incoming and outgoing diamond shipments with precision and care. This is a hands-on, detail-oriented role that sits at the heart of our operations. You’ll be responsible for maintaining the smooth day-to-day flow of the office while upholding our high standards of accuracy and security. With our rapidly growing company, the opportunities for personal and professional growth are enormous. If you're looking for a fast-paced, highly supportive environment where your attention to detail and reliability will truly shine—this is your moment. What you'll do Shipment Handling & Repacking: Accurately handle, inspect, and repack incoming and outgoing diamond shipments in accordance with company protocols and international shipping standards. Operational Support: Work closely with your two team members to manage the daily operations of the office, ensuring all logistics processes run smoothly and efficiently Precision & Security: Maintain the highest level of precision, confidentiality, and security when dealing with high-value goods—attention to detail is non-negotiable in this role. Team Collaboration: Collaborate with senior team members to align on priorities, share insights, and uphold our collective standards of excellence. Process Improvement: Contribute ideas to improve workflows and increase operational efficiency as the company continues to scale rapidly. Growth Mindset: Be proactive, reliable, and open to learning. This role offers strong internal growth potential for individuals who show initiative and dedication. What you'll need for this entry-level role: Strong Attention to Detail Ability to repack/handle goods Team-Oriented Mindset Basic Administrative Skills Trustworthiness & Discretion Highly desirable Experience working in high-security logistics environments, preferably with luxury goods, jewelry, or diamonds. Familiarity with international shipping regulations and customs procedures. Proficiency in basic logistics software or ERP systems (e.g. SAP, NetSuite, or similar). Strong written and verbal communication skills in English; additional languages are a plus. Physically fit and able to handle small manual tasks as part of the shipment handling process. A proactive, solution-oriented attitude with a willingness to grow within a fast-scaling organization. What you'll get: 💸Competitive compensation 🍎Free lunch 🧠 Plenty of opportunities for growth and learning 🚀 Chance to join and contribute to a company during its exponential expansion phase

jobs.title: Freelance Software Tester | Remote in Belgium
jobs.description: Hi there! We're Testlio , a global software testing company that has been helping businesses improve their digital products since 2012. We work with companies around the world to test websites, mobile apps, and online payment systems. Our freelance community helps identify issues and make sure these products work as expected for real customers. Learn more about us at www.testlio.com . About This Opportunity We're looking for people in Italy, Belgium, and Germany to help us test how local payment methods work when paying for advertising on Facebook and Instagram through Meta Ads Manager. Requirements: Location & Payment Method: Italy: Satispay account. Belgium: Wero activated with a Belgian bank account. Germany: Wero activated with a German bank account. Have access to Meta Ads Manager, or be willing to create an account. Have an iOS/Android device or a computer with an updated browser, plus a smartphone with the required payment app. Comfortable following instructions and submitting feedback in English. Available to start ASAP and complete testing by November 16, 2026. Duration: Approximately 1.5 hours. Compensation: Paid hourly testing assignment. Don't have Satispay or Wero yet? You can still apply if you're willing and eligible to set it up before testing. What You'll Do: Follow step-by-step instructions from our testing team. Add a local payment method to Meta Ads Manager. Complete a small advertising payment of approximately €5. Check whether the payment goes through successfully. Report any errors or unexpected behavior, including screenshots when needed. Why do we need local testers? Online payment methods can work differently depending on the country, bank, and device. That's why companies need local people to help check that payments are processed correctly. Your role is to follow simple instructions, complete a small authorized transaction, and tell us whether everything worked as expected. No previous software testing experience is required! Privacy & Security We take the protection of personal and financial information seriously. You'll receive instructions for the assigned testing activities. Never share passwords, full card numbers, or sensitive banking information in your reports. If your profile matches the project requirements, our team will reach out with the next steps. Official recruitment emails will come from a @testlio.com email address, so please keep an eye on your inbox! #LI-REMOTE

We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place. Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths. Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory. If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you. Build and manage QA/QC teams, train staff, and implement standardized testing procedures. Provide technical reports and data analysis to support procurement, production, and R&D decisions. Drive continuous improvement in testing methods, including micro-analysis and advanced fiber testing technologies. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree or above in Textile Engineering, Material Science, or related fields. Proven experience in cashmere or wool fiber testing, with strong knowledge of raw material analysis. Background in either brand-side QA/QC or third-party testing institutions is highly welcomed. Familiarity with international and domestic testing methods (composition, length, color, oil content for down/feather)

Where the SA leads the technical strategy on complex deals, the Field CTO owns the technical narrative across the territory, shapes how the market understands Sigma's architecture, and carries the credibility to win the room when the CTO, CDO, and CISO are all in it. This person does everything a senior SA does, then operates a tier higher: as a peer to enterprise executives, a force multiplier across the entire Solution Engineering team, and a direct line back into Product and Engineering. jobs.description: About the Role We're looking for a FinOps Data Engineer to help drive cost optimization and cloud financial governance across our AWS infrastructure and GCP footprint. You'll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Finance, and Product to find and ship savings, build the tooling necessary to maximize efficiency of every dollar spent in the cloud, and cultivate a culture of cost awareness across engineering teams. This role owns the data side of that mission: the models, pipelines, and analysis that make cost, usage, and margin numbers trustworthy across the company. This is a hands-on engineering role, not an analyst seat. You'll do the schlep work other teams don't have time for, digging into a bucket's access pattern, writing the dbt model or Python pipeline that ships the fix, building the cost-vs-revenue mart that answers a margin question once instead of every time, and chasing a number until it reconciles. Strong communication matters as much as technical depth, you'll regularly explain a savings case or a data model's implications to an engineering team, a finance stakeholder, and a leadership audience in the same week. What You'll Be Responsible For In this role, you'll: Find and ship savings across AWS and GCP: Analyze billing, usage, and cost trends to identify opportunities, rightsizing, storage lifecycle policies, data transfer, and spot/auto-scaling. Take ideas from identification through to a realized dollar figure, not just a recommendation. Build and maintain the FinOps data pipeline: Design and run the BigQuery/dbt models that turn raw billing and usage data (CUR, Storage Lens) into reconciled, trustworthy mart tables, the foundation everything else in FinOps is built on. Build cost-vs-revenue and customer segmentation models: Model unit economics and margin by product line and customer segment, and extend coverage as new products and segments come online. Apply data science to cost and usage data: Build forecasting models, detect anomalies statistically rather than by threshold alone, and quantify savings opportunities (e.g. storage lifecycle, request-cost patterns) with rigor a spreadsheet can't match. Build and maintain cost attribution: Tagging policies, cost allocation, and chargeback/showback so engineering teams can see and own their own spend. This is foundational work other savings work depends on. Automate cost governance: Build automated cost reporting, anomaly detection, and alerting. Write the scripts and infrastructure-as-code (Python, Terraform, Lambda) that enforce cost policy rather than relying on manual review. Partner with engineering on architecture decisions: Bring cost into the room early, cost-efficiencies are cheaper to get right at design than to retrofit. Work with Finance on forecasting and reporting: Support budget tracking and financial KPIs; build dashboards and self-serve analytics engineering and finance can both read. You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have strong AWS expertise and working GCP knowledge, including pricing models, billing structures, and cost optimization mechanics. Have data engineering depth: dbt, BigQuery (or an equivalent modern warehouse), SQL at scale, and data modeling for analytics (dimensional modeling, incremental models, testing). Have data science fundamentals: statistical forecasting, anomaly detection, and experimentation, and know when a rigorous model beats a rule of thumb. Have automation and scripting skills: Python, Terraform/ pulumi, Lambda, or Bash. Ar

jobs.description: About us At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Agentic AI to redefine content creation. Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn't just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too. The role Workflows are how most of the creative on Pencil gets made. A workflow is a visual sequence of steps, covering inputs, generation, brand assets, scoring, branching logic and delivery, that a person builds once and runs again whenever the job repeats, on demand or on a schedule. This role owns that product and the connections that feed it, with one goal: more workflows built and run, by more people, across every customer. You will own Workflows and Integrations. That covers the workflow builder, templates, scheduling and run management, and the steps that workflows are built from. It also covers the platform's third-party connections outside media: digital asset management systems, file storage such as Google Drive, translation services, data services such as Foreplay, and more than a hundred other business tools. You will make those connections part of the workflow itself, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. You will build them on a common framework, so that each new connection is quicker to ship than the last and client teams can build on it for individual clients. You will also own how workflows show up inside Scribble, our creative agent. Agents can already run as steps inside a workflow. The next step is for Scribble to find, build, change and run workflows on a person's behalf and report back as they run, and for a workflow to pause for a person's decision and act on it. You will work closely with the team that builds Scribble, and you will own the workflow experience it works through, so that a workflow behaves the same whether a person or an agent is driving it. When that works, building a workflow stops being a specialist job. Key responsibilities Own the charter for Workflows and Integrations: the durable problem, success metrics, and an explicit in and out scope list. Grow adoption across every customer, measured by the number of workflows built and run and the number of people building them. Own the workflow experience that Scribble works through, so that an agent can find, build, change and run a workflow with the same tools a person uses. Make human review part of the run: a workflow should pause for a person's decision, record it, and continue down the right path. Make runs dependable at volume, with scheduling, run management, failure handling and clear status, so that a team trusts a workflow to run unattended. Own third-party integrations outside media, from digital asset management and file storage to translation and data services, and make them built-in steps in a workflow, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. Set the integration framework and standards that client teams build on when they connect a system for a single client.
